newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen heading lower at start.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen heading lower at start.

text.p: The Dow industrials are expected to head lower at the start of trading Tuesday after yesterday, rallying to their first record close in nearly two months.
But analysts said that even as profit-taking hit the Dow, which surged 143 points to 7214 on Monday, Nasdaq stocks should continue to rally.
"The market must run into some profit-taking," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. He said the Dow could fall up to 150 points in the next few days.
"After pulling back, the Dow should begin to consolidate. Nasdaq will continue to move forward because there is a lot of profit-taking going on. That's good for the broader market," Cardillo said.
Bill Meehan, analyst at Prudential Securities, also said he expected a softer opening, but he said that many investors were waiting for the chance to buy on any pullback.
"I don't think it's unreasonable to expect the unreasonable," he said. "People are waiting to buy, so we can move ahead. We'll still be pretty fat and happy if we can get the Dow up to 8200."
The Tokyo stock market returned from a long holiday weekend in a bullish mood, boosting the benchmark index above the closely watched 20,000 point barrier for the first time since mid-December.
The 225-share Nikkei average surged 666.17 points or 3.41 percent higher to finish at 20,180.92, the highest closing level since 20,413.46 set on December 17.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 65 AT 4520.
The dollar slid against the yen in Tokyo and was off its lows against the mark in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly lower, with the long bond down 10/32 to yield 6.90 percent.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Philip Morris Cos Inc which climbed $3-7/8 or nearly 10 percent on Monday after a favorable U.S. court ruling, was down $1/4 to $43-3/4 while RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp eased $1/8 to $32-1/2 after a $3 jump overnight.
Elsewhere, Intel Corp slipped $1/4 to $162-1/4 following a $4-7/8 advance on Monday while Digital Equipment Corp added $1/8 to $31-3/4.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that legendary investor Warren Buffett once again sounded a dubious note about whether further market advances can be supported.

The New York Times Market Place writes that the Bre-X Minerals fraud, in which a gold find said to be worth billions of dollars turned out to have no gold worth mining, may turn out to be the most costly stock market fraud ever.
